title: Measure the windows per-test-timeout mechanism, and exercise the LCLI-516 guard's failure path (RUNNER_TEMP included)
description:
Filed from LCLI-516's AC#0 residual (note added there). LCLI-516 added a classifier-based single retry to the windows-latest leg of ci.yml's Test step (PR opum-ai/lore-cli#529), keyed on the same signal the ubuntu leg uses (every failing test hung at the per-test budget). Two things it did NOT establish:

(1) The windows arm's ROOT CAUSE. It is established only as DISTINCT from the LCLI-507 Bun epoll/stdio race -- epoll is Linux-only, so the race cannot be it -- and the runner's pre-existing FS/resource-pressure note is a standing hypothesis, never measured for this shape. AC#0 clause (a) is therefore met for ubuntu (LCLI-659) but unmeasured for windows.

(2) The guard's FAILURE PATH is unexercised. The windows suite has passed on every run since the guard landed, so the branch that runs ONLY on failure -- the classifier call, the retry, and `${RUNNER_TEMP}` under `shell: bash` on windows-latest (the repository's first RUNNER_TEMP use on a Windows-executing step) -- has never executed. A guard whose failure path has never run is unproven: if `${RUNNER_TEMP}` does not resolve under MSYS bash, the classifier reads an unreadable log, exits 2, the guard fails CLOSED, and the job reds on the very flake it was added to absorb. The reviewer flagged this at LCLI-545's confirmatory check and could not settle it from the tree.

Suggested approach: make the windows leg reproduce a per-test hang deliberately (an env-gated test that sleeps past the per-test budget) and confirm attempt 1 is retried, attempt 2 runs, and the attempt-1 log is readable at the RUNNER_TEMP path; and capture a real windows occurrence to characterise the mechanism rather than inferring it.

NOT STAMPED: no assignee; opum-doc decides whether it is dispatched.
